org: Microsoft – Office Add-ins data visualization style guidelines
accessNotes: The guideline page (~1,100 words, updated 2025-12) was read in full. It contains no hex codes; it defers to Fluent UI type ramp and neutral palettes. Neutral greys are taken from Fluent UI DefaultPalette.ts and the categorical palette from Fluent UI react-charting colors.ts (secondary sources: the Fluent UI library the guide recommends).
summary: Short principle-based guide for charts inside Office (Excel, etc.) task panes, aligned with the Fluent UI / Segoe look. Emphasis on data ink: no shadows, outlines or 3D; light grey axis labels and thin light gridlines; legend flush-left above the plot; sentence-case titles with an optional all-caps subtitle. It also covers motion (stage axes before data) and accessibility.

colors.categoricalNotes: Guide itself gives no palette: 'Choose colors that follow operating system or application themes rather than hardcoded colors'; points to ColorBrewer and I Want Hue, warns against rainbow. The listed values are Fluent UI react-charting DataVizPalette qualitative 1–10 (cornflower, hotPink, teal, orchid, lightGreen, lightBlue, pumpkin, lime, lilac, gold); colours 11–40 are shades/tints with separate dark-theme variants.
colors.notes: Neutral values are Fluent DefaultPalette (neutralPrimary #323130, neutralSecondary #605e5c, neutralTertiary #a19f9d, neutralQuaternaryAlt #e1dfdd, neutralLight #edebe9); guide only says 'Light grays are most effective for axis labels' and 'for gridlines', dark enough for contrast but not competing with data ink. Fluent semantic dataviz colours: info #015cda, error #c50f1f, warning #f7630c, success #107c10, disabled #dbdbdb. Gradients only when values are bound to colour. Reference images use a blue (#0078d4-like) highlighted series and an orange-red/grey set on light grey background.

typography.fallback: Fluent UI type ramp; any sans-serif with large counters

axisTitle.placement: omitted in examples (unit in subtitle/tick e.g. '50%')

typography.notes: 'In general, use sentence capitalization ... you can use all caps, but all caps should be used sparingly' (example subtitle 'AUGUST - SEPTEMBER 2019' in caps). Use the Fluent UI type ramp (Segoe), or a different typeface to differentiate chart content from UI. 'Use sans-serif typefaces with large counters.'

structure.gridlines: Thin and light grey, secondary to data ink; optionally dynamic just-in-time gridlines on interaction. Example shows faint grid in both directions.
structure.axisLine: Example shows a thin dark x-axis baseline only.
structure.ticks: Small ticks on x axis in example.
structure.zeroLine: Emphasised dark zero line in the % change example.
structure.unitPlacement: % shown on the top tick only ('50%') in example
structure.background: Office/Fluent theme background (light grey in examples)
structure.notes: No drop shadows, heavy outlines, 3D, or unnecessary elements.

legend.placement: top, flush left above the plot; if items don't fit, upper right of plot area, scrollable
legend.directLabels: End-of-line labels with value used in example image
legend.title: no
legend.swatchShape: matches mark: circle for scatter/bubble, line segment for line charts
legend.notes: Only add legends to distinguish series or present scale/value changes.

marks.lines: Thin straight segments (no smoothing) in examples; highlighted series thicker
marks.notes: Avoid 3D unless a value is bound to the third dimension; gradients only when bound to data.

labels.dataLabels: Adequate white space and type variation; algorithms to avoid occlusion/collision.
labels.dates: Full month names / years on x axis

furniture.title: Title top-left creating clear hierarchy; sentence case; subtitle states measure/time span.
furniture.other: Chrome for visualizations built with Fluent UI components.

annotations: Callout box tooltip pointing to a data point (e.g. 'New 3,254') with thin blue border.
interaction: Tooltips surface right of the data point by default, flip left near edges; rich visual feedback; direct manipulation (drag to sort); keyboard-accessible controls; screen reader focus/tooltip announcements. Motion: stage one thing at a time, axes before data ink, groups of ≤4–5 objects, motion in the visualization's coordinate space, no gratuitous animation.
accessibility: Don't use colour as the only channel; add shape, size and texture. Keyboard access to all interactive elements. Adequate text/background contrast for axis labels. Gridlines may be heavier for high-contrast mode.

chartTypes.notes: No chart-type catalogue in the guide.

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend sits flush-left above the plot area by default; move it to the upper-right of the plot (scrollable) only if items don't fit.
distinctiveRules.quote: Flush left above the plot area by default, if all legend items fit above the chart.

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend markers match the mark: line segments for line charts, circles for scatter/bubble.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use line segment legend markers for line charts.

distinctiveRules.rule: Axis labels and gridlines are light grey from the Fluent neutral palette; gridlines thin and light.
distinctiveRules.quote: Light grays are most effective for gridlines.

distinctiveRules.rule: Titles in sentence case using the Segoe/Fluent type ramp; all caps used sparingly (e.g. a caps date-range subtitle).
distinctiveRules.quote: use sentence capitalization ... all caps should be used sparingly

distinctiveRules.rule: No drop shadows, heavy outlines, 3D or decorative gradients on data marks.
distinctiveRules.quote: Avoid the use of drop shadows, heavy outlines, or unnecessary design elements

distinctiveRules.rule: Colours follow the OS/app theme rather than hard-coded values (theme-aware light/dark).
distinctiveRules.quote: Choose colors that follow operating system or application themes rather than hardcoded colors.

distinctiveRules.rule: Tooltips appear to the right of the point and flip left at edges; collision-avoiding labels.
distinctiveRules.quote: a tooltip might surface to the right of a data point by default, but surface to the left if right edges are detected

distinctiveRules.rule: Animate axes before data ink; stage one change at a time, ≤4–5 objects per group.
distinctiveRules.quote: Stage changes to axes before changes to data ink.

distinctiveRules.rule: Default categorical order (Fluent charting): cornflower #637cef, hot pink #e3008c, teal #2aa0a4, orchid #9373c0, green #13a10e, light blue #3a96dd, pumpkin #ca5010.

referenceImages.describes: Anatomy line chart on light grey (#e6e6e6) background. Title 'Current Users' top-left in regular-weight Segoe ~20px, dark grey; all-caps subtitle 'AUGUST - SEPTEMBER 2019' ~11px below. Legend row flush-left above plot with short line-segment markers: yellow, dark navy, orange-red, bright blue (thick), yellow-green. Five straight-segment lines; 'Label Four' bright Office blue (~#0078d4) drawn ~3px thick as the highlighted series, others ~1px. Y axis 0–60 left, no gridlines, thin dark x baseline; x labels 2015–2019. A white callout tooltip with thin blue border reads 'New 3,254' pointing at a point.

'Product review' bold large black Segoe title top-left, regular subtitle '% change in product price, quality and popularity since January'. Light grey background with faint light gridlines both directions (fine grid). Y axis left with ticks -30..50, '%' only on top label '50%'; emphasised dark grey zero line. Three straight lines: grey 'Price', orange-red 'Quality', blue 'Popularity', each direct-labelled at the right end in its colour with signed values (+20%, -20%, -22%); no legend. Month names on x axis, small ticks.
